string-array.name: municipalities_array
string-array.item: Beijing is the capital of China and one of its four municipalities. It is in northern China, beside Hebei province and Tianjin. Mountains surround much of its northern and western sides. The city has a long history and was the capital during several Chinese dynasties. The Forbidden City was home to the Ming and Qing emperors. Other well-known places include the Temple of Heaven, the Summer Palace and the Badaling Great Wall. These places help visitors learn about Chinese history. Today, Beijing is also an important centre for government, culture, international exchange and scientific research.

Shanghai is a municipality on the east coast of China. It is close to the mouth of the Yangtze River and faces the East China Sea. Jiangsu and Zhejiang are its neighbouring provinces. Its short name, Hu, comes from an old fishing tool used in the area. Shanghai became a major trading port in the nineteenth century. The development of Pudong later helped the city grow as a centre for finance and trade. The Huangpu River is an important part of the city. Its coastal location also makes Shanghai an important place for shipping and transport.

Chongqing is a municipality in southwestern China, on the upper reaches of the Yangtze River. Much of its land is made up of hills and mountains. The Yangtze, Jialing and Wujiang are among its main rivers. Chongqing has a long history and served as a wartime capital during the war against Japan. It became a municipality under the central government again in 1997. The municipality includes both busy urban districts and large rural areas. It is the largest of the four municipalities by area. Industry and transport have helped it become an important economic centre in western China.

Tianjin is a municipality in northern China, close to Beijing and the Bohai Sea. The Haihe River passes through the city and flows into the sea. Its rivers and connection to the Grand Canal helped it become an important transport centre. Grain and other goods passed through Tianjin on their way to the capital. The name Tianjin was given during the Ming Dynasty, and a garrison was established there in 1404. The city later developed into a centre for trade and industry. Today, Tianjin Port connects the region with many ports around the world.
